2. idHelpIcon ladder (OptionsIdList.lua:462-472). It is resolved once per instance, as today. The rungs, in order:

   (b) host = d.addonName, accepted only if it is a non-empty string AND the addon-loaded check does not say "no". EXACT CONTRACT. Core.lua minor 10. The `opts` table gains three optional fields; `minWidth`, `minHeight`, `maxWidth`, `maxHeight`, `widthOnly` and `onResize` are unchanged.

`canResize`: `function(frame) -> truthy|falsy`.
- It is read fresh on every OnMouseDown, after the button filter (a button other than left or nil still does nothing) and before the user-placed read and `StartSizing`. It is never cached and never read at mouse-up.
- Falsy: the mouse-down does nothing. `sizing` stays false and `wasPlaced` is not read. The following mouse-up therefore does nothing: no StopMovingOrSizing, no SetUserPlaced, no onResize, no onResizeStop.
- Truthy: exactly the minor-9 behavior.
- A drag that has already started finishes even if the lock flips during the drag, which matches LootHistory's ungated OnMouseUp (Browser.lua:1066-1068).
- A value that is not a function is ignored and the grip always resizes, the same rule as `onResize`.
- It is not wrapped in pcall, the same as onResize: a predicate that raises is a host bug and should reach the error handler.
- It never touches the grip's visibility.

`onResizeStop`: `function(width, height)`.
- It runs exactly once per mouse-up that ends a sizing the grip started. It runs after StopMovingOrSizing, after the user-placed restore and after onResize, with the same `readSize(frame)` values (either may be nil).
- It never runs from OnSizeChanged or after a refused mouse-down. Not wrapped in pcall. A value that is not a function is ignored.

`gripParent`: a frame table, default `frame`.
- The grip is created as `CreateFrame("Button", nil, gripParent)`, anchored `BOTTOMRIGHT` to gripParent at -1,1, and placed at gripParent's frame level + 10.
- Sizing still acts on `frame`: StartSizing, StopMovingOrSizing, bounds, the user-placed flag and the OnSizeChanged hook all stay on `frame`.
- A value that is not a table is ignored. `frame.resizeGrip` is still set on the frame being sized.

RETURN SEMANTICS ARE UNCHANGED. MakeResizable answers the grip or nil, and changes nothing where there is no CreateFrame or `frame` lacks SetResizable or StartSizing. The grip is shown at build. Visibility after that belongs to the host (document this: "the library shows the grip once and never hides it; a host that hides a locked grip owns both SetShown writers, and canResize is the gate either way").

IMPLEMENTATION SHAPE (Core.lua):
- `buildGrip(frame)` becomes `buildGrip(frame, parent)` and reads level and anchor from `parent`.
- `wireGrip(grip, frame, relayout)` becomes `wireGrip(grip, frame, relayout, canResize, onStop)`. The canResize check goes between :618 and :619. `onStop(readSize(frame))` goes after `relayout(...)` at :629.
- MakeResizable (:649-671) resolves the three fields beside `onResize` at :655.
- The library's own callers (DebugLog.lua:689-690, Widgets.lua:512-513, PerfPanel.lua:162-163) pass none of the three fields and keep their minors.

Visible behavior changes on adoption: the grip moves from -2,2 to -1,1, gains a pushed texture, and in MultiMeters grows from 12 to 16 px. Mouse-down now ignores buttons other than left (the hand-rolled grips start on any button), and resize maxima become the size of UIParent where the hosts set none. A resize alone also stops marking the named window user-placed, which is harmless because all three hosts restore geometry from SavedVariables, but it differs from today.

LootHistory behavior change: today's ungated OnMouseUp (Browser.lua:1073-1077) calls SaveWindow and BrowserTable:Refresh even after a locked mouse-down. With canResize, a refused mouse-down leaves the mouse-up inert. This is strictly more correct, but a characterization test that pinned the old mouse-up would need a deliberate update.

MultiMeters bounds: MakeResizable sets bounds once, at build, from opts or the anchor's current size. MultiMeters recomputes them in ApplyResizeBounds (Window_Placement.lua:~108) from the layout. If BuildFrame runs before that, the window briefly cannot shrink below its built size. Pass layout minima, or confirm ApplyConfig always calls ApplyResizeBounds after BuildFrame.

gripParent is an extra field with a single consumer (MultiMeters). If the owner prefers a minimal Core 10 (canResize and onResizeStop only), MultiMeters#58 part 1 becomes will-not-do with this reason recorded, and gripParent is dropped from the contract.

A canResize or onResizeStop that raises is not wrapped in pcall, which matches onResize. A host bug therefore surfaces as a Lua error from the grip's script handler instead of failing silently. That is deliberate, but the doc should state it.

The standard has no rule for how a locked grip looks, so LootHistory (visible and inert) and MultiMeters (hidden) will keep differing. If uniformity is wanted, that ruling goes to WowAddonStandards first (an open-evolution entry), not into this library minor.

MultiMeters runs its own frame mock (tests/mock_frame.lua) rather than the kit's. The library's grip calls more frame methods than the hand-rolled one did, so the host suite may need mock additions before the swap is green.
